responses_archetypeVariants.defender: Take the recoil seriously before dismantling it, because it is doing something — just not what it thinks. The horror is aimed at a picture the button does not contain: bodies, terror, the non-consensual violence of actual killing. Strip those out, which the thought experiment does by stipulation — instantaneous, painless, universal, no survivor left to grieve, no one actually proposing to build the thing — and watch what the horror has left to fasten onto. Nothing in the violence register survives the conditions. What the recoil is still reacting to, once every practical atrocity has been removed, is the bare fact that the experiment ends experience — and reacting to a painless universal cessation with the same intensity as to a massacre is the tell: the objection is not tracking suffering the button causes, because it causes none. It is defending existence as such, the fact of life independent of its content. Name that and the move is made — it is not the cessation but its painlessness that the objection cannot metabolize, because painlessness removes the very thing the horror needed. The button is a scalpel, not a weapon; it exists to cut one question free of every confound and lay it bare: is existence, regardless of what it contains, worth preserving for its own sake? Answer yes and the cost is explicit — the child dying of bone cancer was, on that accounting, 'worth it' for having existed at all. That is the bullet the recoil is quietly biting, and it should be made to see the bullet rather than left to recoil at the picture it has already been relieved of. The genuinely hard version of this objection does not run on horror at all — it grants the painlessness and presses the structural point: that the button overrides the preference of everyone alive who wants to keep living, which is itself a consent-violation in the framework's own terms. That is not a recoil and is not met by naming a conflation; it is the sophisticate's question, answered in that slot, not this one. The defender move stops where the horror is shown to have no object.
